cases.title: Return scalar width from fact lookup
cases.scope: A 32-key mixed numeric/fixed-name persistent P154Facts table and n changing compiler-shaped transfer/update steps; includes setup, whole final-table checksum and teardown. Not a complete compiler stage.
cases.oracle: Baseline calls the unchanged Phase154 fact functions. Root compares old/new outputs; no expected values obtained by executing candidates during preparation.
limitations: Checksum equality is a bounded regression screen, not whole-table structural equivalence or a proof.
Small fixed working set and deterministic trace do not establish whole-compiler coverage.
Machine admission and direct borrowed access must be checked by the root; source scalar return alone does not prove them.
The same capability already exists for P147VLive membership/capacity; this is an application to a different remaining call path, not a new ownership feature.
Only width queries are replaced; arithmetic using the full fact is unchanged.
cases.whatWorkDisappears: Whole P154FCell and P113KFact return lifetimes before width projection disappear; traversal count and ordinary update remain.
cases.method: p155f_bits descends to the requested width at the matching leaf. It applies the existing scalar-query pattern to the Phase154 full-cell fact path.

limitations: Checksum equality is a bounded regression screen, not whole-table structural equivalence or a proof.

cases.whatWorkDisappears: Two fact-tree descents become one existing whole-cell lookup followed by a combined scalar consumer.
cases.method: p155f_combined uses p154f_get once and retains its whole-cell result interface, deliberately isolating query fusion from idea01.

cases.title: Keep a computed hash through reads and update
cases.scope: A 32-key mixed numeric/fixed-name persistent P154Facts table and n changing compiler-shaped transfer/update steps; includes setup, whole final-table checksum and teardown. Not a complete compiler stage.
cases.oracle: Baseline calls the unchanged Phase154 fact functions. Root compares old/new outputs; no expected values obtained by executing candidates during preparation.
limitations: Checksum equality is a bounded regression screen, not whole-table structural equivalence or a proof.

Only four of 32 keys use String hashing; numeric-key hash work is already trivial.

cases.scope: A 32-key mixed numeric/fixed-name persistent P154Facts table and n changing compiler-shaped transfer/update steps; includes setup, whole final-table checksum and teardown. Not a complete compiler stage.

fixture.seed: Exact/bounded facts plus valid Boolean relation/predicate records.
fixture.consumption: Every iteration transfers facts and updates the persistent table; final checksum includes every key, normal-fact field, version, relation and predicate field.
fixture.output: U32 modular checksum as String; n controls the number of changing iterations, not host-side semantics.

measurement.recommendedScreen: Use controls first, then calibrate n in the shared target lane; do not subtract n=0 from measured totals.
mechanismChecks: 01: inspect scalar-result worker admission and absence of returned P154FCell transport.
02: inspect one lookup for the paired consumer.
03: inspect retained hash use and unchanged traversal count.
04: inspect one persistent publication path instead of two.

extraChecks.name: p155f_controls
extraChecks.scope: Finite exact fieldwise controls, separate from timed kernels.
checks: Compare scalar-width and combined width/version queries against original P154 operations for every key and two absent keys.
Compare cached-hash update and original update by exact entire trie structure, collision bucket ordering, names, normal fields, versions, relations and predicates.
Compare batched publication and original publication by the same exact whole-table comparator; repeated oracle-state updates exercise epochs and preserved stale relations.
limitations: Finite states and sizes do not establish a universal equivalence proof.
The timed output remains a checksum; exact control is supplementary and never included in timing.
